subject: Request: short-list & legal snapshot for telemetry subprocessor rotation

Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor short-list & legal snapshot request — planned telemetry partner

Hi Jonas,

Hope you’re well. Quick one from our security team: we were notified that Redwood is planning to route a portion of EU telemetry (edge logging + usage metrics) through a new partner, EdgeRelay Ltd. Before we progress the PO/contract, our security and procurement teams need a short-form package we can review: a one-page short-list of impacted subprocessors (who will see telemetry/metrics for EU tenants), a brief dataflow sketch showing where data will transit, and a legal snapshot (DPA addendum or proposed wording + confirmation of onshore fallback options).

Could you send that over by EOD tomorrow? Our primary concerns are residency (EU routing), temporary access windows, and whether the new partner will have access to any tenant PII or request logs. If you already have a CSV roster or a draft addendum, attaching those would speed things up.

Thanks — Alice

--

Alice — thanks for the note and the checklist. We can do that.

Short answers up front:
- We will provide a CSV short-list of subprocessors that would touch telemetry/metrics for EU tenants and a one-page dataflow sketch.
- EdgeRelay Ltd will be used as a transit/relay for aggregated telemetry (no raw request bodies).
- We’ll include a draft DPA addendum clarifying the scope, encryption controls, access windows, and an onshore fallback option.

Marissa / Kimberly — looping you in for legal & compliance review. Need a quick read on the draft addendum and confirmation on whether the EdgeRelay profile requires a PDP (privacy impact) or SOC2 evidence. Can one of you take the draft and the attached short-list once I pull it?

I’ll pull the inventory and send the CSV + sketch in the next 3–4 hours. If you prefer a synchronous call, I’m available 1–2pm PT.

Best,

Alice — thanks for the patience. Please find the requested short package attached and a short summary below.

Attachments (attached here):
- subprocessor_shortlist.csv (CSV): high-level roster with scope flags (TRANSIT / AGGREGATOR / STORAGE) and residency columns.
- dataflow_sketch.png (PNG): one-page diagram showing telemetry routing for EU tenants plus onshore fallback path.
- dpa_addendum_draft.pdf (PDF): proposed DPA addendum language (covers scope, access windows, encryption-in-transit & at-rest, and onshore fallback).

Summary (TL;DR):
- EdgeRelay Ltd will act as a transit/aggregation partner for non-PII telemetry only (usage counters, latency histograms, anonymized resource IDs).
- No raw request bodies or customer-submitted content will be routed to EdgeRelay.
- Temporary access windows: EdgeRelay will have access only for 30-day rolling windows for troubleshooting (audited, minimum-privilege).
- Onshore fallback: we’ve documented an onshore relay and can failover within 6 hours for EU-regulated tenants; language included in the addendum.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether FinVault needs any additional control evidence (SOC2+bridge, ISO cert, or a custom questionnaire)?
2) If the addendum is acceptable, we can push it to DocuSign — I’ve included a draft link here: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/placeholder (placeholder until final review).

If you want a short call to walk through the sketch, I can do 11:00–12:00 CET today.

Thanks,
